title: Problem Statement and Imports
content: Module documentation describing Erdős Problem #863 on B₂[r] sum sets vs difference sets, with imports for Data.Nat.Basic, Data.Finset.Basic, Data.Finset.Card (finite set combinatorics), Order.Filter.Basic, and Tactic for proof automation. Order.Filter.Basic is imported but Filter.atTop/eventually are never invoked anywhere in the file — no asymptotic or convergence statement is formalized.
mathContext: The module formalizes the question: for B₂[$r$] sets $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ where each integer has at most $r$ representations as $a+b$ ($a \leq b$), and the difference analogue where each nonzero integer has at most $r$ representations as $a - b$, do the asymptotic constants $c_r$ and $c'_r$ differ when $r \geq 2$? The asymptotic constants and any $\varepsilon$-$\delta$/Filter.atTop convergence statement are not formalized in this file; the Filter.Basic import is unused.

title: Sum Representation Count
content: Defines sumRepCount A n as the number of ordered pairs (a, b) in A x A with a ≤ b and a + b = n. This counts the number of ways n can be represented as a sum of two elements from A with the smaller element first. For Sidon sets (B₂[1]), every n has at most one such representation.
mathContext: $\text{sumRepCount}(A, n) = |\{(a, b) \in A \times A : a \leq b \wedge a + b = n\}|$. The ordering constraint $a \leq b$ avoids double-counting: each unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ with $a + b = n$ contributes exactly once (or twice if $a = b = n/2$).

title: B₂[r] Set (Sum Version)
content: A set A is B₂[r] if every natural number n has at most r representations as a + b with a ≤ b, a, b in A. For r = 1 this is the classical Sidon (B₂) property: all pairwise sums are distinct. The maximum size of a B₂[r] set in {1,...,N} is known to be Θ(√(rN)); Cilleruelo, Ruzsa, and Trujillo (2002) showed |A| ≤ (rN)^{1/2} + O(r^{1/2} N^{1/4}).
mathContext: $\text{IsB2r}(A, r) \iff \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\; |\{(a,b) \in A^2 : a \leq b,\; a+b = n\}| \leq r$. The B₂[$r$] condition generalizes the Sidon property by allowing up to $r$ representations per integer.

title: Difference Representation Count
content: Defines diffRepCount A n as the number of pairs (a, b) in A x A with a - b = n (computed over Z). Unlike the sum version, there is no ordering constraint — any pair can produce any nonzero difference. For n ≠ 0, the count equals the number of a in A with a - n in A.
mathContext: $\text{diffRepCount}(A, n) = |\{(a, b) \in A \times A : a - b = n\}|$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. The lack of an ordering constraint means each pair $(a, b)$ with $a \neq b$ contributes to both $n = a - b$ and $-n = b - a$, creating a structural asymmetry with the sum version.

title: Difference B₂[r] Set
content: A set A is a difference B₂[r] set if every nonzero integer n has at most r representations as a - b with a, b in A. The exclusion of n = 0 is essential since (a, a) always gives a - a = 0, contributing |A| representations of 0.
mathContext: $\text{IsDiffB2r}(A, r) \iff \forall n \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\},\; |\{(a,b) \in A^2 : a - b = n\}| \leq r$. The structural difference from the sum version is that subtraction has no natural ordering: $a - b$ and $b - a$ are distinct nonzero values.

title: Containment in {1,...,N}
content: The predicate InRange A N asserts that every element a in A satisfies 1 ≤ a ≤ N. This restricts attention to subsets of the interval {1,...,N}, the standard finite setting for Sidon-type extremal problems.
mathContext: $\text{InRange}(A, N) \iff \forall a \in A,\; 1 \leq a \leq N$. The lower bound $1 \leq a$ excludes $0$, ensuring all elements contribute nontrivially to sums and differences.

title: Maximum B₂[r] Set Sizes
content: Defines maxB2rSize r N and maxDiffB2rSize r N as the maximum cardinalities of B₂[r] (resp. difference B₂[r]) subsets of {1,...,N}. Implementation uses Finset.sup over the powerset of Finset.range(N+1) filtered by the respective properties. The ratio maxB2rSize(r, N)/√N is conjectured to converge to c_r.
mathContext: $\text{maxB2rSize}(r, N) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\},\; \text{IsB2r}(A, r)\}$, similarly for differences. These extremal functions capture the maximum density of B₂[$r$] sets in the finite interval.

title: Classical Sidon Bound: c₁ = c'₁ = 1
content: Comment recording the classical result that for r = 1 (Sidon sets), both the sum and difference B₂[1] sets achieve maximum size ~√N. The upper bound is due to Lindström (1969) and the lower bound follows from Singer's difference set construction (1938) which achieves √N - O(N^{1/4}). This is documented as background in a comment — not stated as an axiom, definition, or theorem in this file.
mathContext: $c_1 = c'_1 = 1$: $\text{maxB2rSize}(1, N) \sim \sqrt{N}$ and $\text{maxDiffB2rSize}(1, N) \sim \sqrt{N}$ as $N \to \infty$. Not formalized in this file: no axiom, definition, or theorem asserts this asymptotic, and Filter.atTop is never used — it appears only in a comment.

title: Erdős Conjecture: c'ᵣ < cᵣ for r ≥ 2
content: The main conjecture: for every r ≥ 2, the asymptotic constants satisfy c'_r < c_r, i.e., the maximum difference B₂[r] set is strictly smaller than the maximum sum B₂[r] set. Erdős's intuition: the ordering constraint a ≤ b in sums is more restrictive than the free pairing in differences, so sums 'waste' fewer representations.
mathContext: $\forall r \geq 2,\; \exists c, c' > 0:\; c' < c \wedge \text{maxB2rSize}(r, N)/\sqrt{N} \to c \wedge \text{maxDiffB2rSize}(r, N)/\sqrt{N} \to c'$ is the informal statement of the conjecture. It is not formalized in this file: no axiom, definition, or theorem states it, and Filter.atTop is never used — the conjecture lives only in this comment.

title: Weak Conjecture: cᵣ ≠ c'ᵣ for Some r ≥ 2
content: The weaker version: there exists some r ≥ 2 for which c_r ≠ c'_r. This does not specify the direction of the inequality. Even this weaker statement is open, as no explicit computation of c_r or c'_r for r ≥ 2 is known. Ruzsa showed c_r ≤ √r and constructions give c_r ≥ √r - o(1), suggesting c_r ~ √r, but analogous bounds for c'_r have not been established with enough precision to separate them.
mathContext: $\exists r \geq 2:\; c_r \neq c'_r$ where $\text{maxB2rSize}(r, N)/\sqrt{N} \to c_r$, $\text{maxDiffB2rSize}(r, N)/\sqrt{N} \to c'_r$. A stepping stone that avoids specifying the direction of the inequality.
